recipes.name: Ground Chicken Taco Burgers
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (1 ounce) package dry taco seasoning mix

steps.text: Preheat the outdoor grill to medium-high heat. Lightly oil the grill grate, and position it about 4 inches from the heat source.

Mix ground chicken, onion, garlic, taco seasoning, and egg together in a bowl until thoroughly blended. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Divide chicken mixture evenly and form into 4 soft patties.

Cook chicken patties on the preheated grill until meat is no longer pink and juices run clear, 5 to 8 minutes per side, depending on thickness. To serve, place each patty on one half of a hamburger bun, top with a slice of cheese, avocado slices, and desired amounts of jalapeño peppers and salsa. Cover with remaining half of bun.

raw_recipe.headline: Ground Chicken Taco Burgers
raw_recipe.description: These Mexican chicken burgers are made with ground chicken, minced onion, garlic, and taco seasoning. Top with pepper Jack, avocado, jalapeños, and salsa.

review.reviewBody: WOW! These were really good burgers. A little hard to handle, and not very pleasing to look at but the taste was 5 stars, easily. EDIT: Wet your hands before you make the patties this helps with the sticky meat.

Delicious and juicy burger! Added 1/2c of bread crumbs after reading some other reviews. I did not use the grill. Browned the burgers on the skillet 2-3 mins on each side then transferred to 325 degree oven for 7 mins. It came out perfectly! I ended up making 5 patties as it seemed too thick.

Delicious, easy and quick recipe for ground chicken. After reading some reviews saying that the mixture was too wet, I decided to use only an egg yolk. The mixture was still sticky so I added 1 T bread crumbs. I made these into 8 small patties and Air fried at 400 for 4 minutes on each side. I served with black bean and rice. Next time I might add some cilantro and maybe some chopped jalapenos as suggested by some reviewers.

This was pretty good! I didn't use an egg, but breadcrumbs are needed because it was fairly loose. I doubled all the spices and added chopped serrano and a jalapeno seasoning for extra heat. Mixed it all up and let it set for about an hour in the fridge before forming into patties and fried on a cast iron grill indoors. Topped it on toasted buns with grilled onions, cheddar, guacamole, tomatoes, bacon, a touch of sour cream and salsa and it was so messy and delicious! Wish I would have added chopped cilantro to the meat! Next time!

I made this last night and it was great!! I jazzed it up a little bit by adding some fresh diced green pepper along with the onion(red) to the chicken mix. I used crushed garlic. I had some home made taco seasoning I used to reduce the sodium, I do recommend using at least 1 1/2TBS of seasoning. I cooked it on the Foreman Grill, lightly oil the grill and the patties on both sides with olive oil to avoid sticking. I didn't make thick patties so it cooks all the way through with out burning the outsides. I cooked it one patty at a time for cooking evenness for 7-8 minutes along with turning as the Foreman tends to cook some areas faster. I will be making this again!! Thanks for the recipe

Made this for dinner tonight. Had a pkg of ground chicken and needed a recipe for what to do with it. I used fresh garlic(wasn't sure if it was to be fresh or the dried). I also added 1/4 cup plain breadcrumbs, as others suggested, with the egg. This made 4 big patties. I cooked them indoors on an electric griddle. I did lightly toast the buns as suggested, I think it adds a nice touch. Topped them with the pepperjack cheese, salsa, lettuce, sliced avacado and french fried jalapenos. They were so moist and flavorful! This recipe is a keeper ! Thanks for sharing!

Very good and easy. To the ground chicken I added one egg, about a cup of bread crumbs, taco seasoning and a pinch of salt and pepper and formed into patties. I grilled the patties on the stove and then melted cheese on top just before serving. I made a guacamole/salsa spread and topped burgers with fresh lettuce and tomatoes. Really great way to eat ground chicken!

I really enjoyed this as did my husband. I too had to add breadcrumbs to this however as it was very gooey. I cooked the burgers on my Foreman grill, and dressed them w/lettuce, tomato, onion, pickled jalapenos, salsa & guacamole. I think this would make a great meatloaf. You could either add breadcrumbs to it or oatmeal to help bind this together. If I were making a meatloaf with this I would add some chopped up jalapenos, anaheim chiles and/or some pasillas. I would also probably top this with a Mexican hot tomato sauce like El Pato (instead of ketchup that some people do with a traditional meatloaf)......

We really liked this recipe. I put the jalapenos directly into the chicken mixture and I did add a bit of panko crumbs to firm it up a little. I cooked them on the stove in a little olive oil because we don't grill and they were beautiful.

Loved these! I used extra lean ground chicken breast, totally omitted the egg....not neccessary, meat is way moist enough. I also sauteed my onion and garlic first, also added a 4 oz. can of diced green chilies and some panko crumbs for binding. Grilled these babies up and served with sliced avacado, pepperjack and some salsa! I went bunless for carb reasons. Tons of flavor here. Thank you!

Just made this for dinner tonight and it rocked!! I did have to add in a small amount of bread crumbs, as my mixture was too wet to hold together (I grind my own chicken). The taste was amazing. I put them on sesame bun with jalapeno slices.

I followed it to the T!!! And it was sooo good! My husband is not a fan of chicken, he loved it so much he told me to add it to the rotation. Yes the meat is sticky but it doesn't need any bread crumbs it cooks perfectly finished moist flavorful. Fixing to make them again tonight.
Coating with bread crumbs made these even better - subtle flavor but yummy burgers!

Good recipe. Coat your hands in cooking oil before making the chicken mixture into patties. I've tried bare hands and wearing gloves and the mixture is very sticky. Canola oil on my hands really helped
Great. I bake mine, no grill needed lots of flavor.

I made something similar using this recipe. Instead of onions and garlic I sliced and seeded one sweet pepper and one jalapeño. Instead of ground chicken I used ground venison. Still did it on the foreman though.
I added cilantro and jalapeño into the chicken mix before cooking. Then I topped it with quest and ate it as a lettuce wrap. Fantastic!
great idea and tasty recipe for using ground chicken

This was a nice quick summer sandwich. Easy to make. I used my gas grill. The kids liked the fact that they could build their own. Everything was good. My patties were a little too wet for the grill. They had kind of crumbled while flipping. Despite appearance, they were quite tasty.
Family liked it. I left out the onion by preference. I added 1c breadcrumbs to firm it up for ease of cooking.
